rationale: Initial characterization of autosomal dominant TAF4-related neurodevelopmental disorder (Janssen et al., 2022) was restricted to eight individuals carrying de novo putative loss-of-function (pLoF) alleles, all of whom presented with intellectual disability, dysmorphic facial features, and behavioral abnormalities. In contrast, genome sequencing in a cohort specifically ascertained for severe sporadic developmental language disorder (DLD) with preserved non-verbal cognitive abilities (non-verbal IQ >= 70, absence of ID and ASD) identified a de novo missense variant in TAF4 (individual 6 in Kennis et al., 2026). Furthermore, related clinical observations (Bassi et al.) document TAF4-related cases presenting with DLD, borderline-low IQ (79), anxiety, and mild dysmorphisms. These findings support the hypothesis that de novo missense alleles expand the phenotypic spectrum of TAF4 variation to include severe language disorder without mandatory global developmental delay or intellectual disability.

evidence.text: Trio-based genome sequencing of 25 individuals with severe sporadic developmental language disorder and preserved non-verbal intelligence (non-verbal IQ >= 70, excluding intellectual disability and autism) identified a likely pathogenic de novo missense variant in TAF4 in individual 6.

new_directions.question_text: Do missense variants in TAF4 cluster in specific functional domains (such as the TAFH or histone-fold domain) compared to evenly distributed truncating mutations?
new_directions.rationale: Evaluating whether missense variants causing isolated DLD perturb specific transcriptional co-factor interactions rather than disrupting overall TFIID complex stability will clarify the molecular basis of phenotypic divergence.

new_directions.question_text: What is the prevalence of de novo TAF4 missense variants across larger multicenter cohorts of isolated developmental language disorder with non-verbal IQ >= 85?
new_directions.rationale: Current evidence relies on small cohorts and single proband occurrences; testing larger cohorts is required to determine the exact penetrance of non-syndromic speech and language phenotypes in TAF4 missense carriers.
